purpose: Travel distance for the rest / back-to-back / 3-in-4 context that the official schedule already makes computable. The official NBA schedule prints venue and city but no coordinate, so coordinates come from Wikipedia's GeoData API (the coordinate printed in each arena article's infobox), not from an NBA page.
source_note: Every row below came from one API call of the form https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&prop=coordinates&colimit=max&format=json&redirects=1&titles=<arena titles>, read on 2026-11-15 between 11:40Z and 11:50Z. The value is the coordinate stored on the English Wikipedia article for that arena. It is a SOURCED value, not an official NBA value, and the site labels it that way.

redirect_noted: The 2026-11-15 query for 'Footprint Center' redirected to 'Mortgage Matchup Center', which is the name the official schedule now uses for the Phoenix venue. The coordinate returned belongs to the redirected article, and both names refer to the same building.
distance_method: Great-circle (haversine) distance in kilometres between the two arenas' coordinates, mean Earth radius 6371.0088 km. This UNDERCOUNTS real travel: it is a straight line, not a flight path, and it ignores the leg from the previous city to the airport. The site labels every distance as a great-circle lower bound.
caveats: Wikipedia is not an official NBA source. Any distance derived here is labelled SECONDARY on every page that prints it.

The coordinate is the building's; teams do not always travel building-to-building, and a neutral-site or relocated game would break the mapping. None of the 27 games in the window is at a neutral site, and each venue the official schedule names matches exactly one arena row.
